canonical_topic: Intrinsic Value and Extrinsic Value of an option
definition: The two components that together make up an option's price: intrinsic value is the payoff from immediate exercise, and extrinsic value is the remaining time value in the option's price.
core_idea: An option's premium splits into intrinsic value (what the buyer would receive by exercising right now) and extrinsic value (the time value, found by subtracting intrinsic value from the current option price).
key_points: Intrinsic Value: the amount of money the option buyer would receive if the option were immediately exercised.
Extrinsic Value: the time value of the option, computed by subtracting intrinsic value from the option's current price.
relationships: Together intrinsic and extrinsic value sum to the option's current price/premium

formulas.name: Extrinsic Value
formulas.formula: Extrinsic Value = Current Option Price − Intrinsic Value

variables.Intrinsic Value: money received if the option were exercised immediately
